info.title: evra-callops
info.description:
**evra-callops** is the orchestration backend for Evra's outbound call center platform.

It manages campaign lifecycle (start / pause / stop), dispatches contacts to the LiveKit
agent worker, processes call outcomes and telemetry, and exposes a full operational API
for companies, campaigns, contacts, calls, SIP trunks, dashboards, and audit events.

**Authentication:**
- Agent-facing endpoints (`/calls/*`, campaign lifecycle) require `X-Webhook-Secret`
- Frontend endpoints require a Supabase JWT Bearer token

post.description: Transitions a campaign from `draft`, `paused`, or `stopped` to `running`. Enqueues all eligible contacts and starts the call dispatcher. Returns 409 if the campaign is already running or in a terminal state (`completed`, `deleted`, `archived`). Returns 422 if the campaign has no configured SIP trunk.

409.description: Conflict — campaign is in an incompatible state for this action

post.description: Pauses a running campaign. The dispatcher stops pulling new contacts but in-progress calls are allowed to finish. Returns 409 if the campaign is not currently running.

409.description: Conflict — campaign is in an incompatible state for this action

post.description: Permanently stops a running or paused campaign. The contact queue is purged and the dispatcher is halted. This action cannot be undone — use `pause` if you intend to resume later. Returns 409 if the campaign is not active.

409.description: Conflict — campaign is in an incompatible state for this action

post.description: Downloads and caches the campaign script audio on the shared disk cache. Called by the dashboard after a campaign is saved so agents can play audio without per-call HTTP fetches. Requires the `X-Webhook-Secret` header.

200.description: Prefetch completed, skipped, or failed (see response body)

get.description:
Returns real-time statistics for a campaign: current status, contact counts by state, number of active calls in progress, and total calls completed today. Suitable for polling from a dashboard.

`auto_paused` is `true` when the campaign was paused automatically by the scheduling window enforcer (outside allowed calling hours) rather than by a manual pause action. It will be automatically resumed when the next allowed window opens.

Retrieves full campaign configuration plus a `summary` of contact statuses and call outcome counts. The summary gives a real-time snapshot of how many contacts are pending, in-progress, dialed, or failed, and how many calls have been placed.

patch.description: Updates campaign configuration fields. Only fields provided in the request body are changed. Cannot change `sip_trunk_id`, `max_concurrent`, or `dialing_speed` while the campaign is running — pause it first. Returns 409 if the campaign is running and a restricted field is included.

post.description: Called by the agent worker at the end of each call to report the business outcome. Updates contact lifecycle, call_records, call_logs, and releases the concurrency slot. Requires the `X-Webhook-Secret` header.

409.description: Call record already exists for this room

post.description: Telephony narrative (SIP, AMD, DTMF, playback) for a completed call. Requires `X-Webhook-Secret`.
LiveKit SDK SessionReport for AI usage metrics. Requires `X-Webhook-Secret`.
Batch of lifecycle or SDK metric events for a completed call. Requires `X-Webhook-Secret`.
Best-effort single milestone update during an active call. Requires `X-Webhook-Secret`.

get.description: Verifies that the service can reach the configured LiveKit server. Returns `connected: true` and the server URL on success, or `connected: false` with an error message if the connection fails.

200.description: Health check result (may indicate unhealthy via `connected: false`)

get.description: Returns all currently active LiveKit rooms. Rooms with zero participants may still appear until they are explicitly deleted or expire.

schema.title: Response List Rooms Livekit Rooms Get

post.description: Creates a new LiveKit room with the given name. If a room with that name already exists, LiveKit returns the existing room.

201.description: Room created (or returned if already exists)

delete.description: Deletes the specified LiveKit room and disconnects all participants. Safe to call on already-deleted rooms.

get.description: Returns all configured SIP outbound trunks registered in LiveKit.

schema.title: Response List Trunks Livekit Trunks Get

post.description: Registers a new SIP outbound trunk in LiveKit with the provided credentials and phone numbers. The trunk can then be referenced by `trunk_id` when placing calls.

422.description: Request body validation error or no fields provided for update

patch.description: Partially updates an existing SIP outbound trunk. Only fields included in the request body are changed. At least one field must be provided — returns 422 otherwise.

422.description: Request body validation error or no fields provided for update

delete.description: Removes the specified SIP outbound trunk from LiveKit. Any future calls referencing this trunk ID will fail.

post.description: Places a one-off outbound SIP test call to verify trunk and carrier connectivity. The request blocks (up to `timeout_seconds`) until the call is answered or fails. `sip_trunk_id` is required — returns 400 if omitted. Always returns HTTP 200; check the `ok` field to determine success.

200.description: Test call result (check `ok` field for success/failure)

post.description:
Endpoint for the LiveKit server to POST real-time room and participant events. Validates the JWT in the `Authorization` header using the LiveKit API secret — returns 401 on failure.

**Events that update session fields:** `room_started` (sets `room_id`, `started_at`), `room_finished` (sets `ended_at`), `participant_joined` / `participant_left` (tracks SIP leg state).

**Events that log an event row only:** `participant_connection_aborted`, `track_published`, `track_unpublished`, `ingress_started`, `ingress_ended`.

Events for rooms with no matching call session are silently ignored.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's identity, profile, and company memberships. Use this to bootstrap the frontend session after login — it provides everything needed to render the user's workspace without additional round-trips.

200.description: User identity, profile, and company list

get.description: Returns all companies the authenticated user belongs to, including contact details and account status. Useful for multi-company users who need to switch workspace context.

200.description: List of companies the user belongs to

get.description: Returns all valid campaign status values used across the platform. Use these to populate status filter dropdowns in campaign list views and validate form inputs.

200.description: Valid campaign status values with display labels

get.description: Returns all valid contact status values. Contacts move through these states as the campaign dispatcher processes them — from `pending` through to `dialed`, `retry`, or terminal states like `do_not_call`.

200.description: Valid contact status values with display labels

get.description: Returns all valid values of call_records.outcome — the result of each dial attempt, matching the DB CHECK constraint. `connected` means the contact answered. `no_answer` and `no_speech` (AMD-detected unavailable machine) represent unanswered calls. `failed` indicates a carrier or SIP error. `hangup` is a mid-call/mid-confirm disconnect and `error` a runtime exception during the call. `voicemail`, `callback`, `opted_out`, `subscribed`, and `lead` are business-relevant outcomes recorded on the same column; see `/lookups/business-dispositions` for the separate, agent-reported disposition vocabulary.

200.description: Valid call outcome values with display labels

get.description: Returns all valid agent outcome values that represent the contact's response or action during the call. `opt_out` removes the contact from future calls. `qualified` and `callback` represent positive engagement.

200.description: Valid agent outcome values with display labels

get.description: Returns all IANA timezone identifiers supported for campaign calling-window scheduling. Use these values in campaign `time_window_start` / `time_window_end` fields.

Returns predefined calling-window presets available for campaign scheduling. Each preset specifies allowed calling hours. Use `business_hours` for standard 8–17 calling or `extended_hours` for earlier/later outreach.

Returns a paginated list of all companies the authenticated user can access. Results are filtered to the user's company memberships. Defaults to `status=active`. Supports search by name and sorting by name, status, or creation date.

post.description: Creates a new company account. The authenticated user is automatically assigned the `admin` role for the new company. Returns 409 if a company with the same name already exists.

get.description: Retrieves full details for a single company. Returns 403 if the authenticated user does not belong to this company (existence is not leaked — the response is identical to a 404 to prevent enumeration).

patch.description: Updates company details. Only fields provided in the request body are changed; omitted fields retain their current values. At least one field must be provided.

post.description: Archives a company, preventing new campaigns from being launched under it. The company and its data remain accessible in read-only mode. Reversible via the restore endpoint.
Restores an archived company to active status, re-enabling campaign creation and dispatching. Works even when the company is archived (the scope check is relaxed for this endpoint).

get.description: Returns a paginated list of campaigns belonging to the company. By default excludes archived and deleted campaigns. Pass `status=archived` to list archived campaigns. Supports search by name and sorting by name, status, or date.

post.description: Creates a new campaign in `draft` status under the specified company. If a `contacts` array is provided, those contacts are imported immediately. Invalid or duplicate phone numbers are counted in `contacts_rejected`. The campaign must be started separately via `POST /campaigns/{id}/start`.

201.description: Campaign created with contact import summary

post.description: Archives a completed or stopped campaign. Archived campaigns are hidden from default list views but their data (contacts, calls, outcomes) is retained for reporting. Returns 409 if the campaign is currently running — stop it first.
Restores an archived campaign back to `draft` status, allowing it to be reconfigured and relaunched. The campaign's contacts and call history are preserved.

Creates a full copy of the campaign configuration in `draft` status with the provided name. Set `include_contacts: true` to also copy all non-DNC contacts into the new campaign as `pending`. Returns the new campaign and the number of contacts copied.

201.description: Duplicated campaign with contact copy count

get.description: Returns a paginated list of contacts enrolled in the campaign. Supports filtering by `status` (pending, in_progress, dialed, retry, failed, do_not_call), `network_provider` (`Vodacom`, `MTN`, `Cell C`, or `unknown` for unclassified/non-SA numbers), and full-text search across first name, last name, and phone number.

parameters.name: network_provider

schema.description: Filter by mobile network provider: `Vodacom`, `MTN`, `Cell C`, or `unknown` for numbers that could not be classified.
schema.title: Network Provider

parameters.description: Filter by mobile network provider: `Vodacom`, `MTN`, `Cell C`, or `unknown` for numbers that could not be classified.

post.description: Adds a single contact to the campaign. The phone number is normalised to E.164 format — returns 422 if the number is invalid. The contact is created in `pending` status and will be dialled when the campaign dispatcher reaches it.

get.description: Returns contact counts grouped by mobile network provider (`Vodacom`, `MTN`, `Cell C`), plus an `unknown` bucket for numbers that could not be classified (non-SA or unrecognised prefix). Optionally narrow to a single contact `status`. Replaces the need for four separate `page_size=1` count calls with the `network_provider` filter.

200.description: Network provider breakdown for the campaign

post.description: Imports multiple contacts into the campaign in a single request. Each contact must have a valid phone number. Invalid numbers are rejected and returned in the `errors` array. No deduplication is performed — use the `/import` endpoint if deduplication is needed.

200.description: Bulk import result with created and rejected counts

post.description: Imports contacts from a structured payload with optional deduplication against existing campaign contacts. When `dedupe: true` (default), contacts with a matching phone number are updated rather than inserted. Returns a unique `import_id` for tracking plus detailed counts of created, updated, duplicate, and rejected contacts.

get.description: Retrieves a single contact record including the contact's last 10 call attempts across all retry cycles. The `recent_calls` array is ordered newest-first and includes outcome, business disposition, talk duration, and timestamp.

200.description: Contact detail with recent call history

patch.description: Updates a contact's name, phone number, or status. Phone numbers are re-normalised to E.164 on update. Status changes must use a valid contact status value from `/lookups/contact-statuses`.

post.description: Sets the contact's status to `archived`, removing it from the active dialling queue. The contact's call history is preserved. Use this to suppress a contact without placing them on the do-not-call list.

Manually re-queues a contact for another dial attempt by setting their status to `retry`. Useful for re-scheduling contacts that failed due to transient errors. The campaign dispatcher will pick them up on the next cycle.

Permanently marks a contact as do-not-call. Sets `status` to `do_not_call` and the `do_not_call` flag to `true`. The contact will never be dialled again, even if the campaign is restarted or the contact is re-imported.

get.description: Returns a paginated, sortable list of all call records across all campaigns belonging to the company. Supports filtering by `outcome` and date range. Optionally narrow to a single campaign with the `campaign_id` query parameter. Each item is enriched with `started_at`/`ended_at` (room join→leave, from the LiveKit session) and `duration_seconds` — the true on-air/billed duration, distinct from the agent-reported `talk_seconds`.

200.description: Paginated call records for the company

get.description: Returns a paginated list of call records for a specific campaign. Supports the same filters and sort options as the company-level calls list. Useful for drilling into a single campaign's call history. Each item includes `started_at`/`ended_at`/`duration_seconds` (on-air room duration) alongside `talk_seconds`.

200.description: Paginated call records for the campaign

get.description: Returns a paginated list of all call attempts for a specific contact across all retry attempts. Useful for viewing the full call history for a single contact and diagnosing why a contact was not reached. Each item includes `started_at`/`ended_at`/`duration_seconds` (on-air room duration) alongside `talk_seconds`.

200.description: Paginated call records for the contact

get.description: Returns every call where the contact pressed 1 at least once during a Lead-Gen campaign: a DOUBLE opt-in (`outcome=lead`) or a SINGLE opt-in (pressed 1, listened, no second press — `business_disposition=single_opt_in`). Each item's `optin` field is `double` or `single` accordingly. `double_optin`/`single_optin` are exact totals across the whole filtered set, independent of the current page. Optionally narrow to one campaign with `campaign_id`.

Returns full detail for a single call record, enriched with the associated contact profile, campaign info, and session timestamps (`started_at`, `ended_at`) sourced from the LiveKit session record, plus `duration_seconds` — the true on-air/billed room duration (join→leave), distinct from the agent-reported `talk_seconds`. Returns 404 if the call does not exist or is out of scope.

200.description: Full call detail with contact and campaign context

get.description: Returns milestone timestamps and precomputed segment durations for a dial attempt, anchored at orchestrator dispatch (dispatched_at).

Returns the ordered sequence of lifecycle and SDK metric events captured during the call session. Events are sourced from both the agent worker (AMD results, DTMF presses, playback steps) and the LiveKit SDK (speech, interruptions, model metrics). Events are ordered by `occurred_at`.

200.description: Ordered list of call session events

get.description: Returns LiveKit Agents SDK telemetry events for this call session, including LLM, STT, and TTS metric events emitted by the agent worker. Events are ordered by `occurred_at`. Useful for cost analysis, latency debugging, and model performance review.

200.description: SDK telemetry events for the call session

get.description: Returns a short-lived URL for downloading the call recording. The URL expires 1 hour after it is issued. Returns 404 if no recording exists for this call (recording may not be available if the call was not connected or if recording was disabled for the campaign).

404.description: No recording available for this call

get.description: Returns all SIP trunks linked to the company. Each trunk represents a telephony gateway used for outbound dialling, and may also be linked to other companies (see `company_ids`) if it's a shared carrier connection. Defaults to `status=active`. The `live` field reflects whether the trunk was reachable the last time its health was checked.

post.description: Creates a new SIP trunk and links it to the company. If `livekit_trunk_id` is provided, the trunk is linked to an existing LiveKit SIP trunk. If `address` and `numbers` are provided instead, a new LiveKit SIP trunk is provisioned automatically. The `auth_password` is stored in the vault and never returned in responses. To share an *existing* sip_trunks row with another company instead of creating a duplicate, use `POST /companies/{company_id}/sip-trunks/{sip_trunk_id}/link`.

post.summary: Link an existing SIP trunk to a company
post.description: Links a SIP trunk you already have access to (via one of its currently-linked companies, or admin) to another company, so both can dial through and manage the same carrier connection. Returns 404 if the trunk doesn't exist or you have no access to any of its currently-linked companies. Idempotent — linking an already-linked company is a no-op.

delete.summary: Unlink a SIP trunk from a company
delete.description: Removes the association between a SIP trunk and a company. The trunk row itself is not deleted and remains available to any other companies still linked to it.

get.description: Retrieves configuration details for a specific SIP trunk by ID. Returns 404 if the trunk does not exist or is out of scope.

patch.description: Updates the display name, from-number, or SIP credentials for a trunk. Any company currently linked to the trunk may update it — changes apply to every company sharing it. The `auth_password` is stored in the vault if provided and never returned. At least one field must be included in the request body.

post.description: Archives a SIP trunk. Archived trunks cannot be assigned to campaigns. The trunk remains in the database (and linked to all its companies); its history is preserved.

Dispatches a real outbound call through the SIP trunk to verify it is operational. The call is placed to the `phone` number provided in the request body. Always returns HTTP 200 — check the `ok` field to determine whether the call was dispatched successfully. The `room_name` can be used to correlate LiveKit events for the test call.

get.description: Queries LiveKit to verify the SIP trunk is registered and reachable. Updates the `live` flag on the trunk record. Returns `status: healthy` if the trunk is found in LiveKit, `not_found` if it is missing, or `error` if the LiveKit query failed. Use this before starting a campaign to confirm the trunk is ready.

Returns high-level operational metrics for the company. By default covers the current calendar day in UTC; use `from_date` / `to_date` to query historical windows. Optionally filter to a single campaign with `campaign_id`. `active_calls` reflects the live count of in-progress calls from the in-memory concurrency tracker.

200.description: Aggregated operational metrics for the company

get.description: Returns real-time operational state: which campaigns are currently running, how many calls are active right now (from the in-memory concurrency tracker), and the contact queue breakdown by status. Poll this endpoint every 5–10 seconds to power a live dashboard.

Returns aggregated call outcome and business disposition counts for the specified date range. `outcomes` reflects the telephony result (connected, voicemail, failed, etc.). `business_dispositions` reflects the contact's response during the call (subscribe, opt_out, callback, etc.). Use this to build outcome breakdown charts and disposition funnels.

200.description: Aggregated outcome and business disposition counts

get.description: Returns a time-series of call volume metrics grouped by `hour`, `day`, or `week`. Each bucket in `series` contains the total call count, connected count, and failed count for that period. Use this to render call volume trend charts. Defaults to `day` grouping.

Returns per-campaign performance statistics including total calls, connected count, opt-out count, failed count, and average talk time in seconds. All campaigns for the company are included regardless of status. Use this to compare campaign effectiveness side-by-side.

`by_outcome` gives a raw tally of every `outcome` value seen for the campaign (e.g. `connected`, `subscribed`, `lead`, `opted_out`, `no_answer`, `voicemail`, `failed`) so callers aren't limited to the handful of pre-aggregated columns above. `total_talk_seconds` and `answered_calls` (calls with talk_seconds > 0) are provided for reference, and `total_cost` is the authoritative sum of each call's persisted `cost` (ZAR) — callers no longer need to derive their own cost/CPL estimate from talk time.

get.summary: Call-level insights: daily series, hour-of-day distribution, talk-time distribution, recent calls
get.description: Replaces raw per-call polling for dashboard analytics widgets that need more than outcome counts: a per-day series (calls/transferred/talk-time/cost/outcome breakdown) for sparklines and trend charts, a 24-bucket hour-of-day call distribution (`hourly_distribution`, index 0 = midnight UTC) for a 'busiest hours' chart, a talk-time histogram (`talk_distribution`), and the last 8 calls (`recent`, each with its own `cost`) for a live feed. Each daily bucket's `total_cost` is the sum of the persisted per-call `cost` (ZAR). Bounded to the last `days` days (default 30, max 90) so this stays a cheap, poll-friendly endpoint — it deliberately does NOT return every call ever made.

200.description: Call-level insight data for the last `days` days

get.description: Returns conversation intent metrics for a single campaign, broken down by day, script step, and intent name. Intents are tracked each time a contact reaches a decision point in the script. Also returns the total number of connected calls for the queried period. Supports filtering by a single `date` or a `from_date`/`to_date` range.

200.description: Campaign intent funnel metrics with connected call total

get.description: Returns a company-wide roll-up of conversation intent metrics across all campaigns. Each row identifies the campaign, day, script step, and intent name, making it easy to compare funnel performance across campaigns side-by-side.

200.description: Company-wide intent funnel metrics grouped by campaign

get.description: Returns all saved dashboard templates for the company. By default excludes archived templates. The `is_default` flag indicates which template is the active default for the given `default_scope` (`company` or `user`).

post.description: Creates a new dashboard template with the specified widget configuration. Set `default_scope` to `company` to make it the default for all users in the company, or `user` to make it the default for the creating user only. Setting `is_default: true` replaces any existing default for that scope.

get.description: Retrieves a single dashboard template by ID, including its full widget configuration.

patch.description: Updates an existing dashboard template's name, widget configuration, or default settings. Only fields provided in the request body are changed.

post.description: Archives the template, hiding it from the default list without deleting it. If this template was the current default for any scope, the default is cleared.

Sets this template as the default dashboard view for the specified `scope` (`company` or `user`). Only one template can be the default per scope — calling this automatically clears the previous default for the same scope.

200.description: Template set as default for the specified scope

get.description: Returns a paginated audit trail of security-relevant events such as logins, permission changes, and configuration updates. Scoped to the authenticated user's company. Supports filtering by date range and searching by exact event type.

Returns a paginated audit log of all platform events for the company, including campaign lifecycle changes, contact imports, and configuration updates. This is an alias for `/security-logs` and returns the same data from the same table.

post.description: Calls the configured TTS provider to synthesise speech from `text`. Returns a signed URL to the generated audio file and its duration. Use this to preview how a campaign script will sound before saving it. Returns 501 if no TTS provider is configured and 502 if the upstream TTS service fails.

Persists audio metadata — URL, text, voice, and duration — against a campaign. Typically called after `generate` once the caller is satisfied with the preview. The `audio_url` should be a durable storage URL (not the temporary signed URL from `generate`). Returns the full saved audio record including its assigned `id`.

audio.text: Hi, this is a reminder about your appointment tomorrow at 2pm.

get.description: Returns saved script audio records. Pass `company_id` as a query parameter to retrieve all audio across every campaign in a company (requires company membership). Omit it to filter by `campaign_id` via the standard pagination query. Results are ordered by `created_at` descending by default.

200.description: Paginated list of script audio records

items.text: Hi, this is a reminder about your appointment tomorrow at 2pm.

post.summary: Save a script to the reusable library
post.description: Saves script `text` (optionally with the `voice_id` it was generated with, the resulting `audio_url`, and a display `campaign_name`) to a global, cross-campaign library. Used to power 'reuse a previous script' pickers. Not scoped to a company or campaign — any authenticated user can save and list entries.

script.text: Hi, this is a reminder about your appointment tomorrow at 2pm.

get.description: Returns saved scripts from the global reuse library, newest first.

items.text: Hi, this is a reminder about your appointment tomorrow at 2pm.

get.description: Returns global platform settings, currently just the carrier cost-per-minute rate (ZAR) used to price every call. Readable by any authenticated user.

patch.description: Updates the carrier cost-per-minute rate (ZAR). Admins only — returns 403 for non-admin users. The new rate takes effect immediately for calls priced after this request (an in-process cache is invalidated on write); it does not retroactively reprice already-completed calls.

get.description: Returns `{"status": "ok"}` when the service is up. Used by load balancers and readiness probes.

business_disposition.title: Business Disposition

campaign_id.title: Campaign Id
campaign_id.description: Accepted in POST for traceability; stored on call_sessions / call_records, not call_session_reports.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: Accepted in POST; not persisted to call_session_reports.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Accepted in POST; not persisted to call_session_reports.

sip_attributes.title: Sip Attributes
sip_attributes.description: SIP participant attributes snapshot from LiveKit.

sip_call_status_history.title: Sip Call Status History
sip_call_status_history.description: Ordered SIP status transitions during the call.

CallReportBody.title: CallReportBody
CallReportBody.description: Telephony narrative from the agent `_build_call_report()` payload.

room_name.title: Room Name
room_name.description: LiveKit room name associated with this call report.

call_report.description: Telephony narrative built by the agent (AMD, SIP, DTMF, playback).

auto_paused.title: Auto Paused
auto_paused.description: True when the campaign was automatically paused by the scheduling window enforcer rather than a manual action.

active_calls.title: Active Calls
active_calls.description: Number of calls currently in progress for this campaign.

queued.title: Queued
queued.description: Total contacts waiting to be dialed (pending + retry).

pending.title: Pending
pending.description: Contacts that have not yet been attempted.

in_progress.title: In Progress
in_progress.description: Contacts whose call is currently being handled by the agent.

dialed.title: Dialed
dialed.description: Contacts that have been reached (answered calls).

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Contacts whose call attempts all failed (no answer, busy, error) with no remaining retries.

retry.title: Retry
retry.description: Contacts scheduled for a retry attempt.

completed_today.title: Completed Today
completed_today.description: Total calls completed (any terminal outcome) since midnight UTC today.

status.title: Status
status.description: Current lifecycle status of the campaign. One of: `draft`, `running`, `paused`, `stopped`, `completed`, `archived`.

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.description: List of phone numbers assigned to this trunk in E.164 format.

name.title: Name
name.description: Unique name for the new LiveKit room.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Destination phone number in E.164 format.

sip_trunk_id.title: Sip Trunk Id
sip_trunk_id.description: LiveKit SIP trunk ID to use for the call. Required — returns 400 if omitted.

room_name.title: Room Name
room_name.description: LiveKit room name to create for this test call. Auto-generated from timestamp if omitted.

participant_identity.title: Participant Identity
participant_identity.description: Identity string for the SIP participant in LiveKit.

participant_name.title: Participant Name
participant_name.description: Display name for the SIP participant.

from_number.title: From Number
from_number.description: Caller ID (from number) in E.164 format. Uses trunk default if omitted.

wait_until_answered.title: Wait Until Answered
wait_until_answered.description: If true, the request blocks until the call is answered or times out.

krisp_enabled.title: Krisp Enabled
krisp_enabled.description: Enable Krisp noise cancellation on the LiveKit track.

timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the call to be answered before returning a timeout error.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: True if the room was successfully deleted.

room_name.title: Room Name
room_name.description: Name of the room that was deleted.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: True if the trunk was successfully deleted.

trunk_id.title: Trunk Id
trunk_id.description: ID of the trunk that was deleted.

connected.title: Connected
connected.description: True if the service can reach the LiveKit server.

url.title: Url
url.description: LiveKit server WebSocket URL being checked.

error.title: Error
error.description: Error message if the connection check failed. `null` when connected.

room_name.title: Room Name
room_name.description: LiveKit room name associated with this usage report.

sdk_report.description: LiveKit Agents SDK SessionReport serialisation. Omitted for script-only calls.

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.description: Phone numbers assigned to this trunk in E.164 format.

auth_username.title: Auth Username
auth_username.description: SIP authentication username used when placing calls through this trunk. Password is never returned.

num_participants.title: Num Participants
num_participants.description: Current number of participants connected to the room.

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: Per-model usage breakdown; callops aggregates into typed columns.

events.title: Events
events.description: Non-metric session events from SDK (metrics excluded in to_dict).

SdkUsageEntry.title: SdkUsageEntry
SdkUsageEntry.description: One entry from LiveKit SessionReport `usage` array.

ok.title: Ok
ok.description: True if the call was successfully placed and answered.

room_name.title: Room Name
room_name.description: LiveKit room name used for the test call.

sip_trunk_id.title: Sip Trunk Id
sip_trunk_id.description: SIP trunk ID used for the call.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Destination phone number that was dialed.

participant_identity.title: Participant Identity
participant_identity.description: Identity of the SIP participant as registered in LiveKit.

sip_status_code.title: Sip Status Code
sip_status_code.description: SIP response code from the carrier. Only present on failure (e.g. 486 Busy Here, 480 Temporarily Unavailable).

sip_status.title: Sip Status
sip_status.description: Human-readable SIP status corresponding to `sip_status_code`. Only present on failure.

message.title: Message
message.description: Error or informational message. Present when `ok` is false.

name.title: Name
name.description: New human-readable name for the trunk. Omit to leave unchanged.

address.title: Address
address.description: New SIP server address. Omit to leave unchanged.

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.description: Replacement list of E.164 phone numbers. Omit to leave unchanged.

auth_username.title: Auth Username
auth_username.description: New SIP auth username. Omit to leave unchanged.

auth_password.title: Auth Password
auth_password.description: New SIP auth password. Omit to leave unchanged.
